test_title: PYST 20: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 13 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following changes was introduced in 2024 under the Companies Act amendments to enhance corporate social responsibility (CSR) transparency in India?

options.text: Exemption of companies with a turnover below ₹500 crore from CSR obligations
Reduction in the minimum CSR spending threshold for all eligible companies
Requirement for at least 50% of board members to be CSR specialists
Mandatory quarterly CSR reporting accompanied by independent audits

solution:
The correct answer is __**Mandatory quarterly CSR reporting accompanied by independent audits**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 2024, the Indian government amended the Companies Act to improve **Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) transparency**.
 
• The amendment introduced **mandatory quarterly CSR reporting** for eligible companies to ensure regular updates on CSR activities.
 
• Independent audits of the CSR reports were made **compulsory** to enhance credibility and accountability.
 
• The change aims to address issues of non-compliance, misuse of CSR funds, and ensure alignment of CSR activities with their intended social objectives.
 
• This step is part of broader efforts to encourage **responsible corporate governance** and increase trust among stakeholders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR):**

 
 
• CSR refers to the practices where businesses voluntarily contribute to sustainable development by delivering economic, social, and environmental benefits.
 
• In India, Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 mandates CSR spending for companies meeting certain financial thresholds.
 
• Eligible companies must spend at least 2% of their average net profit of the last 3 years on CSR activities.
 
 
 
• **Independent Audits:**
 
 
• Independent audits involve third-party examination of financial or operational processes to ensure compliance and accuracy.
 
• In the context of CSR, these audits validate the effectiveness and alignment of CSR projects with prescribed norms.
 
 
 
• **CSR Reporting:**
 
 
• CSR reporting involves documenting and disclosing information about a company’s CSR activities, expenditures, and outcomes.
 
• Quarterly reporting ensures transparency and provides regular updates to stakeholders about the company’s contribution to social development.
 
 
 
• **Impact of CSR Amendments:**
 
 
• Improves corporate accountability and stakeholder confidence.
 
• Encourages companies to align their CSR initiatives with national development goals.
 
• Addresses misuse or underutilization of CSR funds by ensuring stricter compliance.
